source_refs.note: The three sex-determination systems (PDF 103-105); Figure 18.13 is replaced by the original diagram. The printed 'Y carrying egg' is read as W.

blocks.text: In Drosophila, mammals and most other vertebrates the sex chromosome pair is a rod-shaped X and a hook-shaped Y: females are XX and males XY. Drosophila has 3 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes; humans have 22 pairs of autosomes and 1 pair of sex chromosomes.

Females are homogametic: all their eggs carry one X. Males are heterogametic: half their sperm carry an X and half a Y. A sperm with X fertilizing an egg gives an XX zygote that develops female sex organs; a sperm with Y gives an XY zygote that develops male sex organs.

blocks.alt: Three panels. XX-XY (humans, Drosophila): XX female, XY male; eggs all X, sperm X or Y; XX female and XY male in equal numbers. XX-XO (grasshopper): female XX with 24 chromosomes, male XO with 23; sperm X or O; XX female and XO male. ZW-ZZ (birds): ZW female, ZZ male; eggs Z or W, sperm all Z; ZZ male and ZW female. Each gives 1 female : 1 male.
blocks.caption: The XX-XY, XX-XO and ZW-ZZ systems (original diagram after Figure 18.13).
blocks.long_description: In the XX-XY system females make only X eggs and males make X and Y sperm in equal numbers, so the sperm decides the sex: X sperm give XX daughters and Y sperm XY sons. In the XX-XO system of grasshoppers males have a single X; half the sperm carry X and half carry no sex chromosome (nullo gametes), giving XX females with 24 chromosomes and XO males with 23. In the ZW-ZZ system of birds the female is ZW and makes Z and W eggs, the male ZZ makes only Z sperm, so the egg decides: Z eggs give ZZ males and W eggs ZW females.

blocks.text: This is found in some insects. The grasshopper has 22 autosomes (11 pairs). The male has 23 chromosomes in total, because its sex chromosome 'pair' is XO: only one X and no Y. It forms two kinds of sperm, half with an X and half with no sex chromosome; a gamete with no sex chromosome is a nullo gamete. The female has 24 chromosomes with XX, and all her eggs carry one X. An X sperm gives an XX female and a nullo sperm an XO male.

This is common in birds. The number of autosomes differs between birds, but the sex chromosomes are ZW in females and ZZ in males. The female makes two kinds of egg, half with Z and half with W, while all the male's sperm carry Z. A Z-carrying egg fertilized by a sperm gives a male (ZZ); a W-carrying egg gives a female (ZW).

blocks.title: Note on the printed text
blocks.text: The book prints 'When a Y carrying egg is fertilized ... offspring is female' for birds; in the ZW-ZZ system the egg carries W, not Y.

blocks.prompt: In birds, which parent decides the sex of the chick, and why?
blocks.explanation: The mother: she is ZW and makes Z and W eggs, while the father (ZZ) makes only Z sperm.

items: XX-XY (humans, Drosophila): male heterogametic; sperm decides.
XX-XO (grasshopper): male XO, 23 chromosomes; nullo sperm.
